_: A whole SCENE as ONE picture, where every other tool here draws a piece. The camp is drawn rather than carved out of a tileset — the user's call: 'build it not using the tile sets and just use art and then make objects clickable on it' — so what this file holds is the camp, and anything else a player LOOKS at rather than walks through.
_rules: (1) The COMPOSITION is load-bearing, because objects on it are CLICKED: say where each thing stands and keep the middle of the ground OPEN, or there is nowhere to put the character. (2) NO PEOPLE. The hero is drawn on top out of his own art, and a painted one is a second hero who never moves. (3) It is a BACKGROUND, so `no_background` is false and nothing may be a frame, a border or a UI panel. (4) Colours by exclusion as everywhere else, and the zone's own words: the camp is green meadow grass under near-black cliff rock.
_size: 688x384 is the 16:9 ceiling for `create_image_pro`, and at 2x it covers a 1376x768 stage. Bigger is not on offer.

camp.say: A busy lived-in CAMP on a wide shelf at a cave mouth, a game background seen from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE looking down. THE CAMERA IS PULLED WELL BACK and the view is WIDE, so everything is SMALL with room between things. Across the TOP QUARTER a wall of near-black purple-brown cliff rock runs the full width, a tall narrow SPLIT torn through the middle. OUT OF IT POURS WARM GOLD LIGHT, cream-gold at its core, burnt orange where it spills on the ground. NOT violet, NOT cold. Tight either side of the split are FOUR hollows CHISELLED into the rock in TWO VERTICAL COLUMNS, jagged-rimmed, gripped by blackened iron claws, empty and dark. THE GROUND IS OLD AND HEAVILY WORN AND THAT IS THE POINT. It is NOT a clean lawn. Green grass survives only in ragged islands at the edges and between things; everywhere people stand or walk it is TRODDEN AWAY to bare packed pale-brown earth in wide irregular patches with soft ragged edges. MANY narrow dirt PATHS, uneven and meandering and branching, are beaten across it from the split to every object and from each object to the next, crossing and rejoining. EVERY OBJECT SITS IN ITS OWN PATCH OF BARE TRODDEN EARTH, settled slightly INTO the ground, grass growing against its base, a soft dark contact shadow beneath it. NOTHING RESTS ON UNBROKEN GRASS. Grey ash round the fire, dark slag round the furnace, wood chips round the benches. On it, well spread and at UNEVEN angles: FAR LEFT a squat stone furnace with a glowing mouth and an iron anvil on a stump; a work bench with a vice and a tall shelf of jars; CENTRE a campfire of charred logs in a ring of stones; RIGHT of it an upright loom and a hide on a rack; FAR RIGHT an iron pot on a tripod and a tool table; along the RIGHT EDGE FIVE small shelters of patched canvas and boards, each a different shape. Weathered timber, blackened iron, dull canvas. NOT houses, NOT masonry, NOT a person, NOT text.

climb_fissure.say: A worked-out MINE cut down through near-black rock. It is a CUTAWAY CROSS-SECTION, drawn as a game background seen SIDE ON and STRAIGHT ON as if the ground had been sliced open with a knife and you are looking at the cut face. Solid rock fills the picture edge to edge, and cut through it a chain of open chambers joined by narrow sloping passages STEPS DOWNWARD from the TOP LEFT corner to the BOTTOM RIGHT corner, each chamber lower than the one before it, so the whole picture reads as a descent. It is DIM: the chambers are only a shade lighter than the mass around them, and the only bright things are small. NOT a map, NOT a diagram, NOT a plan, NOT a chart, NOT seen from above, NOT a frame, NOT a border, NOT a UI panel, NOT a sheet of separate pieces. NO PEOPLE, no creatures, no text, no letters, no numbers, no icons, no arrows. The mass is VERY DARK warm purple-brown rock, almost black, NOT pale, NOT grey, NOT sandy, NOT olive, NOT green. Rotted timber props lean in the chambers, some snapped, and grey cobweb hangs in the corners. ONE small candle burns in ONE of the middle chambers and throws a soft warm gold pool of light onto the rock immediately around it and nowhere else; every other chamber is unlit. NOT violet, NOT blue, NOT cold.

_seen: The FIRST round asked the split for violet and got it, and the user's answer was that the glow is the TITLE SCREEN's — measured off `shots/desktop-title.png`, that is pale cream-gold #fcde6f at the core, amber #f0a94b out from it and burnt orange #e08f37 where it washes the rock. The sockets came back as four evenly spread PORTHOLES; they are asked as two VERTICAL pairs tight to the split, chiselled and iron-clawed and no two alike, with `NOT portholes` in the exclusions. The hero reads right at x4 against a scene at x2 — x3 is small and x5 is big.
_limit: `create_image_pro` refuses a `description` over 2000 CHARACTERS, before billing. A scene's ask is long by nature — it places every object — so it runs close to that, and the cut always comes out of the exclusions rather than the composition.
_worlds: climb_fissure / climb_prismatic / climb_demonic are the three WORLDS in cross-section, drawn when the climb's tabs were worlds. The tabs are DEPTH now (climb_act1..3) and these are unused — kept for the socket panel, which wants to show what four crystals compose to. Do not regenerate them; do not delete them without asking.
